note:
Duration of residence is calculated based on number of days, and a new year does not occur until 364 days become 365 days. This means that if a person has been recorded in the Swedish population register for 729 days (1 year and 364 days), that person ends up in the group Duration of residence 0–1 years. If the person has been recorded in the population register for 730 days, the person ends up in the group Duration of residence 2–3 years. The breakdown of other groups works in a similar way, which means that a person must have a duration of residence of at least 3,650 days to end up in the group Duration of residence 10– years. 
  
Ahead of the year 2000, considerable changes were made to the Register of Education to improve quality, with a new nomenclature and a number of new sources, which led to a break in the time series. For this reason, comparisons with prior years must be made with great caution. For more information see: [Quality improvement in the Register of Education, 2000 (in Swedish)](https://www.scb.se/hitta-statistik/statistik-efter-amne/utbildning-samt-forskning-inom-hogskolan/befolkningens-utbildning-och-studiedeltagande/befolkningens-utbildning/produktrelaterat/Fordjupad-information/kvalitetshojningen-i-utbildningsregistret-ar-2000/).

label.AA0003FJ: Proportion of sick pay out of net income, percent
label.AA0003FK: Proportion of sickness and activity allowance out of net income, percent

AA0003FI:
The numerator consists of the sum of sick pay, sickness and activity allowance, unemployment benefit, income support, introductory allowance and foothold allowance. The denominator consists of net income (the sum of all taxable and tax-free income minus taxes and other negative transfer payments). Age bracket 20–64 years. Due to non-response in the collection of income support data for 2011 and onwards, “Proportion of sick pay, sickness and activity allowance, etc. out of net income” for the country and county is only based on the municipalities that submitted complete income support data. As of 2009, unemployment benefit includes activity support and development allowance in addition to unemployment benefit paid out of an unemployment insurance fund. 
  
Source: [Income and tax statistics](https://www.scb.se/HE0110-EN) 
  
Source: [STATIV database](http://www.scb.se/stativ)
AA0003FJ:
The numerator consists of aggregated sick pay. The denominator consists of net income (the sum of all taxable and tax-free income minus taxes and other negative transfer payments). Age bracket 20–64 years. 
  
Source: [Income and tax statistics](https://www.scb.se/HE0110-EN)
AA0003FK:
The numerator consists of aggregated sickness and activity allowance. The denominator consists of net income (the sum of all taxable and tax-free income minus taxes and other negative transfer payments). Age bracket 20–64 years. 
  
Source: [Income and tax statistics](https://www.scb.se/HE0110-EN)
AA0003FL:
The numerator consists of aggregated unemployment benefit. The denominator consists of net income (the sum of all taxable and tax-free income minus taxes and other negative transfer payments). As of 2009, unemployment benefit includes activity support and development allowance in addition to unemployment benefit paid out of an unemployment insurance fund. Age bracket 20–64 years. 
  
Source: [Income and tax statistics](https://www.scb.se/HE0110-EN) 
  
Source: [STATIV database](http://www.scb.se/stativ)
AA0003FM:
The numerator consists of aggregated income support. The denominator consists of net income (the sum of all taxable and tax-free income minus taxes and other negative transfer payments). Age bracket 20–64 years. Due to non-response in the collection of income support data for 2011 and onwards, “Proportion of income support out of net income” for the country and county is only based on the municipalities that submitted complete income support data. For further details please see the website of the National Board of Health and Welfare. 
  
Source: [Income and tax statistics](https://www.scb.se/HE0110-EN) 
  
Source: [STATIV database](http://www.scb.se/stativ)
AA0003FN:
The numerator consists of aggregated introductory allowance. The denominator consists of net income (the sum of all taxable and tax-free income minus taxes and other negative transfer payments). Age bracket 20–64 years. A municipality may grant introductory allowance to refugees and certain other immigrants who have been received in a municipality as part of the municipal refugee reception process. The municipality determines the size of the introductory allowance. Not all municipalities use the possibility of granting introductory allowance to refugees. This is the case for around 50 municipalities in 2007. In some municipalities, introductory allowance is included in income support. 
  
As of 2012, introductory allowance is no longer included in the the National Board of Health and Welfare’s collection for financial assistance statistics, even though disbursements may continue for as long as introduction lasts. 
  
Source: [Income and tax statistics](https://www.scb.se/HE0110-EN) 
  
Source: [STATIV database](http://www.scb.se/stativ)
AA0003FV:
The numerator consists of aggregated foothold allowance. The denominator consists of net income (the sum of all taxable and tax-free income minus taxes and other negative transfer payments). Age bracket 20–64 years. 
  
Source: [Income and tax statistics](https://www.scb.se/HE0110-EN)
